plugin.name: area_map
plugin.author: Mark
plugin.purpose: Maps the rooms you walk through inside each Oerthe map square

muclient.script:
-- Bump whenever the mapping logic changes: shown at load and in 'amap', and -- saved with every trace row, so a trace shows which version decided what. local BUILD = "2026-10-16x"
-- Every room and exit is stamped with the build that last confirmed it -- (created it, or saw it again while walking). When a build fixes a mapping -- bug that could have saved bad rooms or exits, raise MIN_TRUSTED_BUILD to -- it: on load, area rooms not confirmed since then are dropped (after a -- backup) and get remapped as you walk. Overland tiles and rooms with notes -- are always kept. Builds compare as strings, so keep the "YYYY-MM-DDx" form. local MIN_TRUSTED_BUILD = "2026-10-16f"
local WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ID = "26a4ca2758d503d86efe902e" -- mush_windows local MW_BROADCAST_PROMPT = 1 local MW_BROADCAST_PROMPT_CHANGED = 2
local FONT_ID = "amap_font" local FONT_NAME = "Courier New" local FONT_SIZE = 9 local CELL = 36 -- grid spacing in pixels local BOX = 18 -- room box size local EDGE_INSET = 6 -- keep hotspots clear of winframe's resize strips
-- BGR colours local BG_COLOUR = 0x000000 local TEXT_COLOUR = 0xC0C0C0 local LOST_COLOUR = 0x4080FF local ROOM_FILL = 0x707070 local DARK_FILL = 0x2A2A2A local CURRENT_FILL = 0x00A5FF local ROOM_BORDER = 0xD0D0D0 local LINK_COLOUR = 0xB0B0B0 local UNEXPLORED_COLOUR = 0x505050 local HIDDEN_COLOUR = 0x80E080 local DOOR_COLOUR = 0x3030FF local WALL_COLOUR = 0x2020B0 local UPDOWN_COLOUR = 0xFFFFFF local NOTE_COLOUR = 0x00FFFF local BOUNDARY_COLOUR = 0xFF80E0 -- an exit into another sub-area local ID_FONT_ID = "amap_id_font" local ID_COLOUR = 0x00D7FF local BUTTON_BG = 0x333333 local BUTTON_BORDER = 0x888888 local BUTTON_TEXT = 0xFFFFFF
local PEN_SOLID, PEN_DOT = 0, 2
-- Directions ----------------------------------------------------------------
local DIRS = { n = { dx = 0, dy = -1, long = "north", rev = "s" }, ne = { dx = 1, dy = -1, long = "northeast", rev = "sw" }, e = { dx = 1, dy = 0, long = "east", rev = "w" }, se = { dx = 1, dy = 1, long = "southeast", rev = "nw" }, s = { dx = 0, dy = 1, long = "south", rev = "n" }, sw = { dx = -1, dy = 1, long = "southwest", rev = "ne" }, w = { dx = -1, dy = 0, long = "west", rev = "e" }, nw = { dx = -1, dy = -1, long = "northwest", rev = "se" }, u = { long = "up", rev = "d" }, d = { long = "down", rev = "u" }, } local PLANAR = { "n", "ne", "e", "se", "s", "sw", "w", "nw" }
-- Any spelling of a direction -> its short form. local DIR_WORDS = {} for short, info in pairs(DIRS) do DIR_WORDS[short] = short DIR_WORDS[info.long] = short end for _, pair in ipairs{ { "north-east", "ne" }, { "north-west", "nw" }, { "south-east", "se" }, { "south-west", "sw" } } do DIR_WORDS[pair[1]] = pair[2] end
local LOOK_WORDS = { l = true, look = true }
-- Looking into a neighbouring room shows that room, which is not where you are. local PEER_WORDS = { peer = true }
-- First words of commands that never move you. Anything else that isn't a -- direction is treated as a possible (maybe hidden) exit, e.g. "jump down". local NON_MOVE_VERBS = {} for word in ([[ say tell reply shout whisper emote yell ask o open close lock unlock get take drop put give i inv inventory eq equipment sc score exa examine x read wield unwield wear remove kill k cast brief verbose prompt who help hp quit save glance search buy sell list value consider con follow party skills spells time date news mail note bank deposit withdraw balance wimpy alias chat pwho finger last nick unalias unnick dotimes wait stand sit rest rescue assist absorb abilities accept bind throw shoot drink eat fill change increase decrease entangle hone light language offer powerup refill scalp slice tag thaw freeze store receive train keep unkeep unlock fgreet ftell fshatter fs distill attach detach cook set join deliver mine shape crush fish bait salt create breakdo spike smoke view use wield roll ]]):gmatch("%S+") do NON_MOVE_VERBS[word] = true end
-- Commands that take you somewhere fixed wherever you use them: never saved -- as an exit, even when they happen to land nearby. local TELEPORT_WORDS = { recall = true, home = true, teleport = true, transport = true, summon = true }
-- What the game prints instead of a room when it's too dark to see. local DARK_PATTERNS = { "^A dark room%.$", "^It is too dark", "^It's too dark", }
local FAILURE_PATTERNS = { "^What%?$", "^There is no such exit%.$", "^Maybe you should look for another exit%.$", "^You do not think you can go there%.$", "^The .+ is closed%.$", "^.+ stops you from going %a+%.$", -- a guard: "A palace guard stops you from going west." }
-- Runtime state -------------------------------------------------------------
local rooms = {} -- id -> { id, sx, sy, name, desc, exits = set, doors = { dir = closed? }, note } local links = {} -- from id -> { [command] = { to = id, hidden = bool } } local nextId = 1 local current = nil -- id of the room you're in, nil if unknown/lost local lastKnown = nil -- last room you were definitely in (drawn while lost) local lostCount = 0 -- how many rooms matched when you got lost local square = { x = nil, y = nil }
local buffer = {} -- lines received since the last prompt local skipLines = 0 -- prompt lines still to come after the broadcast line local cmdQueue = {} -- { text =, t =, requeued = } local pagerActive = false -- the game is showing "--More--": the next send pages on local promptSpec = nil -- { regexes = { rex, ... }, last = index of the broadcast line } local warnedNoPrompt = false local lastDebug = nil local traceOn = false -- amap trace: print a line per move local showIds = false -- amap ids: draw room numbers on the map local mergeLog = {} -- "#drop->#keep" for merges made while handling this prompt local mapChanged = false -- something to redraw even though no room was seen
local db = nil local mapWin = nil local drawn = nil -- layout of the last draw, for hotspots: { pos =, cx =, cy = } local panX, panY = 0, 0 -- how far the view is dragged from the room it's centred on local panFor = nil -- the room the drag applies to: moving elsewhere re-centres local panStart = nil -- { mx, my, px, py } while dragging
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Small helpers -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
local function Note(msg) ColourNote("orange", "", "[area_map] " .. msg) end
local function PluginDir() local dir = GetPluginInfo(GetPluginID(), 20) or "" if dir ~= "" and dir:sub(-1) ~= "/" and dir:sub(-1) ~= "\\" then dir = dir .. "/" end return dir end
local function Trim(s) return (s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
local function CollapseSpaces(s) return Trim((s:gsub("%s+", " "))) end
local function SetToString(set) local keys = {} for k in pairs(set) do keys[#keys + 1] = k end table.sort(keys) return table.concat(keys, ",") end
local function StringToSet(s) local set = {} for k in (s or ""):gmatch("[^,]+") do set[k] = true end return set end
local function DoorsToString(doors) local parts = {} for dir, closed in pairs(doors) do parts[#parts + 1] = dir .. "=" .. (closed and "c" or "o") end table.sort(parts) return table.concat(parts, ",") end
local function StringToDoors(s) local doors = {} for dir, state in (s or ""):gmatch("([^,=]+)=([co])") do doors[dir] = (state == "c") end return doors end
local function SameSquare(room, sx, sy) return room.sx == sx and room.sy == sy end
local function SquareLabel(sx, sy) if sx == nil and sy == nil then return "?" end return tostring(sx or "?") .. "," .. tostring(sy or "?") end
-- How many rooms each square holds, kept up to date as rooms come and go. local squareCounts = {} -- SquareLabel -> count
local function CountRoom(room, delta) local key = SquareLabel(room.sx, room.sy) squareCounts[key] = (squareCounts[key] or 0) + delta end
local function RoomsInSquare(sx, sy) return squareCounts[SquareLabel(sx, sy)] or 0 end
-- Squares marked with 'amap irregular': areas whose rooms don't sit on a -- grid (a long hall beside small rooms, a path around that's longer on one -- side than the other). There, grid positions prove nothing, so rooms are -- matched by the paths between them instead (see TryJoinByPath). local irregular = {} -- SquareLabel -> true
local function IsIrregular(sx, sy) return irregular[SquareLabel(sx, sy)] == true end
-- An overland map tile: every overland square is a single room, while an -- area fills its square with many. (A new area's first room looks the same -- until a second room in its square is mapped.) local function IsOverland(room) return RoomsInSquare(room.sx, room.sy) == 1 end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Storage (SQLite) -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
local statements = {} -- sql -> prepared statement, reused
local function DbRun(sql, ...) local stmt = statements[sql] if not stmt then stmt = db:prepare(sql) if not stmt then Note("database error: " .. db:errmsg()) return end statements[sql] = stmt end stmt:bind_values(...) stmt:step() stmt:reset() end
local function SaveRoom(room) mapVersion = (mapVersion or 0) + 1 DbRun("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO rooms (id, sq_x, sq_y, name, descr, exits, doors, note, dark, noexits, build, subarea) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", room.id, room.sx, room.sy, room.name, room.desc, SetToString(room.exits), DoorsToString(room.doors), room.note, room.dark and 1 or 0, SetToString(room.noexits or {}), room.build, room.subarea) end
local function SaveLink(fromId, cmd, link) mapVersion = (mapVersion or 0) + 1 DbRun("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO exits (from_id, cmd, to_id, hidden, build, boundary) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", fromId, cmd, link.to, link.hidden and 1 or 0, link.build, link.boundary and 1 or 0) end
-- Marks a room as confirmed by this build (walked through, created, updated). local function StampRoom(room) if room.build ~= BUILD then room.build = BUILD SaveRoom(room) end end
-- Every exit in a brief room line is a direction (or one of these few -- words), so other lines ending in brackets aren't rooms: a channel message -- "[Chat] Bashers: fill pouch (when outdoor)", or a who list's -- "GRiXiS the Guardian of the House of Midiar (evil)". local BRIEF_EXIT_WORDS = { enter = true, out = true, ["in"] = true, exit = true, leave = true }
local function ValidBriefExits(text) if text == "" or text == "no exits" then return true end for token in (text .. ","):gmatch("([^,]*),") do token = Trim(token):gsub("^|(.*)|$", "%1"):lower() if not (DIR_WORDS[token] or BRIEF_EXIT_WORDS[token]) then return false end end return true end
-- Builds before 2026-10-16k read any line ending in brackets as a brief -- room: "(no exits)" became an exit called "no exits", and chat or who-list -- lines ("... (evil)") became rooms. The first is cleaned up; brief-only -- rooms whose exits can't be real are deleted (with their exits) at load. function RepairMisreadRooms() local bad = {} for id, room in pairs(rooms) do if room.exits["no exits"] then room.exits["no exits"] = nil SaveRoom(room) end -- Only rooms seen just in brief mode: a verbose exit list can name -- unusual exits ("portal"). if not room.desc and not ValidBriefExits(SetToString(room.exits)) then bad[#bad + 1] = id end end table.sort(bad) for _, id in ipairs(bad) do local room = rooms[id] Note("removed room #" .. id .. " \"" .. tostring(room.name or "?") .. "\": it was a misread line, not a room.") rooms[id] = nil CountRoom(room, -1) DbRun("DELETE FROM rooms WHERE id = ?", id) DbRun("DELETE FROM exits WHERE from_id = ? OR to_id = ?", id, id) end end
-- The game's own aliases and nicknames (its 'alias' and 'nick' commands), -- learned from their listings and from new definitions as you send them. -- The plugin only sees what you type, and the game expands it, so "ep" has -- to be read as "enter portal" to tell a move from a fight command. gameWords = { alias = {}, nick = {} }
local function OpenDb() db = sqlite3.open(PluginDir() .. "area_map.db") -- Every write used to wait for the disk (slow, especially under Wine). -- WAL with synchronous=NORMAL only waits at checkpoints, and still can't -- corrupt the database if MUSHclient crashes. db:exec("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;") db:exec[[ CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rooms ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sq_x INTEGER, sq_y INTEGER, name TEXT, descr TEXT, exits TEXT, doors TEXT, note TEXT ); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exits ( from_id INTEGER, cmd TEXT, to_id INTEGER, hidden INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (from_id, cmd) ); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS rooms_square ON rooms (sq_x, sq_y); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trace ( n INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, t TEXT, cmd TEXT, from_id INTEGER, to_id INTEGER, sq_x INTEGER, sq_y INTEGER, seen TEXT, decision TEXT ); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS game_words ( kind TEXT, name TEXT, expansion TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (kind, name) ); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS squares ( sq_x INTEGER, sq_y INTEGER, irregular INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (sq_x, sq_y) ); ]]
-- Added after the trace table first shipped; fails harmlessly if present. db:exec("ALTER TABLE trace ADD COLUMN build TEXT") db:exec("ALTER TABLE rooms ADD COLUMN dark INTEGER") db:exec("ALTER TABLE rooms ADD COLUMN noexits TEXT") db:exec("ALTER TABLE rooms ADD COLUMN build TEXT") db:exec("ALTER TABLE exits ADD COLUMN build TEXT") db:exec("ALTER TABLE exits ADD COLUMN boundary INTEGER") db:exec("ALTER TABLE rooms ADD COLUMN subarea TEXT")
for row in db:nrows("SELECT * FROM rooms") do rooms[row.id] = { id = row.id, sx = row.sq_x, sy = row.sq_y, name = row.name, desc = row.descr, exits = StringToSet(row.exits), doors = StringToDoors(row.doors), note = row.note, dark = row.dark == 1, noexits = StringToSet(row.noexits), build = row.build, subarea = row.subarea, } CountRoom(rooms[row.id], 1) if row.id >= nextId then nextId = row.id + 1 end end -- Never reuse a room number, even after rooms are forgotten, so a number -- in the trace always means the same room. for row in db:nrows("SELECT MAX(MAX(IFNULL(from_id, 0)), MAX(IFNULL(to_id, 0))) AS top FROM trace") do if row.top and row.top >= nextId then nextId = row.top + 1 end end
RepairMisreadRooms()
for row in db:nrows("SELECT * FROM game_words") do if gameWords[row.kind] then gameWords[row.kind][row.name] = row.expansion end end
for row in db:nrows("SELECT * FROM squares WHERE irregular = 1") do irregular[SquareLabel(row.sq_x, row.sq_y)] = true end
for row in db:nrows("SELECT * FROM exits") do links[row.from_id] = links[row.from_id] or {} links[row.from_id][row.cmd] = { to = row.to_id, hidden = row.hidden == 1, build = row.build, boundary = row.boundary == 1 or nil } end
-- Builds before 2026-10-16m saved an unlisted command that led to a new -- room as an exit however far away it went (a blue door across the -- world); those are teleports, so they go. for fromId, cmds in pairs(links) do for cmd, link in pairs(cmds) do local a, b = rooms[fromId], rooms[link.to] if link.hidden and not DIRS[cmd] and a and b and a.sx and b.sx and a.sy and b.sy and (math.abs(a.sx - b.sx) > 1 or math.abs(a.sy - b.sy) > 1) then cmds[cmd] = nil DbRun("DELETE FROM exits WHERE from_id = ? AND cmd = ?", fromId, cmd) end end end end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Rooms and links -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
local function NewRoom(obs, sx, sy) local room = { id = nextId, sx = sx, sy = sy, name = obs.name, desc = obs.desc, exits = {}, doors = {}, noexits = {}, dark = obs.dark or nil, build = BUILD, } nextId = nextId + 1 for e in pairs(obs.exits) do room.exits[e] = true end for d, closed in pairs(obs.doors) do room.doors[d] = closed end rooms[room.id] = room CountRoom(room, 1) SaveRoom(room) return room end
-- Fills in whatever this sighting adds: the name or description from the -- other mode, exits, and door states. local function UpdateRoom(room, obs) if obs.dark then return end local changed = false if room.dark then room.dark = nil; changed = true end -- seen lit at last if obs.name and not room.name then room.name = obs.name; changed = true end if obs.desc and not room.desc then room.desc = obs.desc; changed = true end for e in pairs(obs.exits) do if not room.exits[e] then room.exits[e] = true; changed = true end end for d, closed in pairs(obs.doors) do if room.doors[d] ~= closed then room.doors[d] = closed; changed = true end end -- Brief mode only marks closed doors (|w|), so a known door listed -- plainly has been opened. if obs.mode == "brief" then for d in pairs(obs.exits) do if room.doors[d] == true and obs.doors[d] == nil then room.doors[d] = false; changed = true end end end if changed then room.build = BUILD SaveRoom(room) end end
local function SetLink(fromId, cmd, toId, hidden) -- A move always goes somewhere else; an exit into the same room is a -- tracking mistake, never saved. if fromId == toId and DIRS[cmd] then return end links[fromId] = links[fromId] or {} local link = links[fromId][cmd] if link and link.to == toId and link.hidden == hidden and link.build == BUILD then return end -- A sub-area boundary stays one while the exit leads to the same room. local boundary = link and link.to == toId and link.boundary or nil link = { to = toId, hidden = hidden, build = BUILD, boundary = boundary } links[fromId][cmd] = link SaveLink(fromId, cmd, link) end
local function DeleteRoom(id) mapVersion = (mapVersion or 0) + 1 if rooms[id] then CountRoom(rooms[id], -1) end rooms[id] = nil links[id] = nil for _, cmds in pairs(links) do for cmd, link in pairs(cmds) do if link.to == id then cmds[cmd] = nil end end end DbRun("DELETE FROM rooms WHERE id = ?", id) DbRun("DELETE FROM exits WHERE from_id = ? OR to_id = ?", id, id) if current == id then current = nil end if lastKnown == id then lastKnown = nil end end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Matching -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Exit lists may only differ by doors: verbose mode leaves a closed door's -- exit out of the list. local function ExitsCompatible(room, obs) -- A dark room shows no exits, so it can't contradict anything. if obs.dark or room.dark then return true end for e in pairs(obs.exits) do if not room.exits[e] and room.doors[e] == nil and obs.doors[e] == nil then return false end end for e in pairs(room.exits) do if not obs.exits[e] and room.doors[e] == nil and obs.doors[e] == nil then return false end end return true end
local function NameCompatible(room, obs) return not obs.name or not room.name or obs.name == room.name end
-- Nothing contradicts: a room seen only in brief mode is compatible with a -- verbose sighting, since one has only a name and the other only a description. local function Compatible(room, obs) return ExitsCompatible(room, obs) and NameCompatible(room, obs) and (not obs.desc or not room.desc or obs.desc == room.desc) end
-- Positively the same text: needed whenever there's no path to go by. local function Recognised(room, obs) -- Every dark room looks the same: never recognised by text, only by path. if obs.dark or room.dark then return false end if not ExitsCompatible(room, obs) then return false end return (obs.name ~= nil and obs.name == room.name) or (obs.desc ~= nil and obs.desc == room.desc) end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Correcting old data -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Folds drop into keep: text, exits, doors, note, and every link from or to it. local function MergeRooms(keep, drop) keep.name = keep.name or drop.name keep.desc = keep.desc or drop.desc keep.note = keep.note or drop.note for e in pairs(drop.exits) do keep.exits[e] = true end for d, closed in pairs(drop.doors) do if keep.doors[d] == nil then keep.doors[d] = closed end end keep.build = BUILD SaveRoom(keep)
keep.subarea = keep.subarea or drop.subarea local function carry(fromId, cmd, old) local new = links[fromId] and links[fromId][cmd] if new and old.boundary and not new.boundary then new.boundary = true SaveLink(fromId, cmd, new) end end for cmd, link in pairs(links[drop.id] or {}) do local to = (link.to == drop.id) and keep.id or link.to if not (links[keep.id] and links[keep.id][cmd]) then SetLink(keep.id, cmd, to, link.hidden) carry(keep.id, cmd, link) end end for fromId, cmds in pairs(links) do if fromId ~= drop.id then for cmd, link in pairs(cmds) do if link.to == drop.id then SetLink(fromId, cmd, keep.id, link.hidden) carry(fromId, cmd, link) end end end end
mergeLog[#mergeLog + 1] = "#" .. drop.id .. "->#" .. keep.id if current == drop.id then current = keep.id end if lastKnown == drop.id then lastKnown = keep.id end DeleteRoom(drop.id) end
-- An overland square is a single room, so if every room in a square is the -- same room by its text and exits, they're copies of one overland tile made -- before it could be recognised, and get merged. Rooms linked to each other -- are never copies (two "Main Street (e,w)" side by side in a new town). -- Returns how many rooms were merged away. local function MergeDuplicatesInSquare(sx, sy) if RoomsInSquare(sx, sy) < 2 then return 0 end local list, inSquare = {}, {} for _, room in pairs(rooms) do if SameSquare(room, sx, sy) then list[#list + 1] = room inSquare[room.id] = true end end table.sort(list, function(a, b) return a.id < b.id end) local keep = list[1] for i = 2, #list do if not (Recognised(keep, list[i]) and Recognised(list[i], keep)) then return 0 end end for _, room in ipairs(list) do for _, link in pairs(links[room.id] or {}) do if inSquare[link.to] then return 0 end end end for i = 2, #list do MergeRooms(keep, list[i]) end return #list - 1 end
-- Defined further down (needs Layout); declared here for MergeAllDuplicates. local TryJoin
local function MergeAllDuplicates() local squares = {} for _, room in pairs(rooms) do squares[SquareLabel(room.sx, room.sy)] = { room.sx, room.sy } end local merged = 0 db:exec("BEGIN") for _, sq in pairs(squares) do merged = merged + MergeDuplicatesInSquare(sq[1], sq[2]) end -- Then join pieces of areas mapped from different entrances, until -- nothing more joins. for _ = 1, 5 do local ids = {} for id in pairs(rooms) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end table.sort(ids) local joinedThisPass = 0 for _, id in ipairs(ids) do if rooms[id] then local n = TryJoin(id) joinedThisPass = joinedThisPass + n end end merged = merged + joinedThisPass if joinedThisPass == 0 then break end end db:exec("COMMIT") return merged end
-- Places rooms on a grid outward from startId, following compass exits -- (not across a sub-area boundary: a sub-area is laid out on its own). -- Positions are worked out fresh each time rather than stored, so rooms that -- don't fit the geometry only ever collide far away from you. It carries on -- into neighbouring squares, since an area can span several. With -- skipOverland, overland tiles are left out (the room you start from is -- always placed). local function Layout(startId, radius, skipOverland) local pos = { [startId] = { 0, 0 } } local cellAt = { ["0,0"] = startId } local queue, head = { startId }, 1 while queue[head] do local id = queue[head] head = head + 1 do local p = pos[id] for _, d in ipairs(PLANAR) do local link = links[id] and links[id][d] if link and rooms[link.to] and not pos[link.to] and not link.boundary and not (skipOverland and IsOverland(rooms[link.to])) then local x, y = p[1] + DIRS[d].dx, p[2] + DIRS[d].dy local key = x .. "," .. y if not cellAt[key] and math.abs(x) <= radius and math.abs(y) <= radius then pos[link.to] = { x, y } cellAt[key] = link.to queue[#queue + 1] = link.to end end end end end return pos, cellAt end
-- Irregular squares are drawn by fitting every exit at once instead of -- stepping from room to room. Each exit keeps its room exactly on the line -- of its direction (a "ne" street stays a diagonal) and at least one step -- away; it may be longer, though as short as it can. So where a way around -- is longer on one side, the short side stretches instead of two rooms -- landing on one spot. Then rooms snap to the grid; one landing on a taken -- cell moves to the nearest free one. -- -- The whole area (up to its sub-area boundaries) is laid out at once from -- its lowest-numbered room and kept until the map changes, so it looks the -- same from every room and the view just moves as you walk. When a room is -- added, the others start from where they were, so they hardly move. -- (Drawing only: matching never uses these positions.) local IRREGULAR_SIDE = 300 -- cost of an exit running off its line local IRREGULAR_SHORT = 30 -- cost of an exit shorter than a step (longer costs 1) local IRREGULAR_ROUNDS = 20 local IRREGULAR_CROSS = 40 -- cost of two unrelated exits crossing on the map local IRREGULAR_ON_LINE = 400 -- cost of a room sitting on an exit's line (it looks connected) local IRREGULAR_BEND = 20 -- per cell squared an exit is bent or short, when untangling -- Cells per step ('amap spread'): an irregular area is drawn spread out, -- so a loop that doesn't add up has room to stretch and rooms can sit -- between the usual spots instead of on top of each other. irregularScale = 2
mapVersion = 0 -- bumped whenever a room or exit changes local irregularCache = {} -- room id -> { version =, pos =, fx =, fy = } for its area local lastFit = {} -- room id -> { x, y }: last unsnapped spot, to start from
local function SolveIrregular(startId) -- The area: rooms joined by compass exits either way, not across a -- boundary, overland left out. local incoming = {} for fromId, cmds in pairs(links) do for _, d in ipairs(PLANAR) do local link = cmds[d] if link and not link.boundary then incoming[link.to] = incoming[link.to] or {} incoming[link.to][#incoming[link.to] + 1] = { fromId, d } end end end local inArea, members = { [startId] = true }, { startId } local head = 1 while members[head] do local id = members[head] head = head + 1 local near = {} for _, d in ipairs(PLANAR) do local link = links[id] and links[id][d] if link and not link.boundary then near[#near + 1] = link.to end end for _, inc in ipairs(incoming[id] or {}) do near[#near + 1] = inc[1] end for _, other in ipairs(near) do if rooms[other] and not inArea[other] and not IsOverland(rooms[other]) then inArea[other] = true members[#members + 1] = other end end end table.sort(members) local rootId = members[1]
-- Starting spots: where each room was last time; new rooms one step from -- a neighbour that has one (stepping out from the root, as on a grid). local fx, fy = {}, {} local order = { rootId } local placed = { [rootId] = true } if lastFit[rootId] then fx[rootId], fy[rootId] = lastFit[rootId][1], lastFit[rootId][2] else fx[rootId], fy[rootId] = 0, 0 end head = 1 while order[head] do local id = order[head] head = head + 1 local function reach(to, dx, dy) if inArea[to] and not placed[to] then placed[to] = true if lastFit[to] then fx[to], fy[to] = lastFit[to][1], lastFit[to][2] else fx[to], fy[to] = fx[id] + dx * irregularScale, fy[id] + dy * irregularScale end order[#order + 1] = to end end for _, d in ipairs(PLANAR) do local link = links[id] and links[id][d] if link and not link.boundary then reach(link.to, DIRS[d].dx, DIRS[d].dy) end end for _, inc in ipairs(incoming[id] or {}) do reach(inc[1], -DIRS[inc[2]].dx, -DIRS[inc[2]].dy) end end
local edges = {} for _, id in ipairs(order) do for _, d in ipairs(PLANAR) do local link = links[id] and links[id][d] if link and not link.boundary and inArea[link.to] and link.to ~= id then edges[#edges + 1] = { id, link.to, DIRS[d].dx, DIRS[d].dy } end end end
-- The best fit of all the exits at once (least squares): each exit wants -- its room one step away in its direction. Being off the line or shorter -- than a step costs a lot, being longer only a little, so the short side -- of a loop that doesn't add up stretches, spread evenly along it. Solved -- with conjugate gradients, then again with the costs updated for which -- exits came out short, a few times over. The root stays at its spot. local index = {} for i, id in ipairs(order) do index[id] = i end local geo = {} for k, e in ipairs(edges) do local len = math.sqrt(e[3] * e[3] + e[4] * e[4]) geo[k] = { ux = e[3] / len, uy = e[4] / len, len = len * irregularScale, w = 1 } end local function apply(px, py, outx, outy) for i = 1, #order do outx[i], outy[i] = 0, 0 end for k, e in ipairs(edges) do local g = geo[k] local a, b = index[e[1]], index[e[2]] local dx, dy = px[b] - px[a], py[b] - py[a] local along = g.ux * dx + g.uy * dy local side = -g.uy * dx + g.ux * dy local fxv = g.w * along * g.ux - IRREGULAR_SIDE * side * g.uy local fyv = g.w * along * g.uy + IRREGULAR_SIDE * side * g.ux outx[b], outy[b] = outx[b] + fxv, outy[b] + fyv outx[a], outy[a] = outx[a] - fxv, outy[a] - fyv end outx[1], outy[1] = 0, 0 -- the root end local px, py = {}, {} for i, id in ipairs(order) do px[i], py[i] = fx[id] - fx[rootId], fy[id] - fy[rootId] end for _ = 1, IRREGULAR_ROUNDS do local bx, by = {}, {} for i = 1, #order do bx[i], by[i] = 0, 0 end for k, e in ipairs(edges) do local g = geo[k] local a, b = index[e[1]], index[e[2]] local gx, gy = g.w * g.len * g.ux, g.w * g.len * g.uy bx[b], by[b] = bx[b] + gx, by[b] + gy bx[a], by[a] = bx[a] - gx, by[a] - gy end bx[1], by[1] = 0, 0 local ax, ay = {}, {} apply(px, py, ax, ay) local rx, ry, dxv, dyv = {}, {}, {}, {} local rr = 0 for i = 1, #order do rx[i], ry[i] = bx[i] - ax[i], by[i] - ay[i] dxv[i], dyv[i] = rx[i], ry[i] rr = rr + rx[i] * rx[i] + ry[i] * ry[i] end for _ = 1, 4 * #order + 20 do if rr < 1e-10 then break end apply(dxv, dyv, ax, ay) local dAd = 0 for i = 1, #order do dAd = dAd + dxv[i] * ax[i] + dyv[i] * ay[i] end if dAd <= 0 then break end local alpha = rr / dAd local rr2 = 0 for i = 1, #order do px[i], py[i] = px[i] + alpha * dxv[i], py[i] + alpha * dyv[i] rx[i], ry[i] = rx[i] - alpha * ax[i], ry[i] - alpha * ay[i] rr2 = rr2 + rx[i] * rx[i] + ry[i] * ry[i] end local beta = rr2 / rr rr = rr2 for i = 1, #order do dxv[i], dyv[i] = rx[i] + beta * dxv[i], ry[i] + beta * dyv[i] end end -- Exits that came out shorter than a step cost more next round. for k, e in ipairs(edges) do local g = geo[k] local a, b = index[e[1]], index[e[2]] local along = g.ux * (px[b] - px[a]) + g.uy * (py[b] - py[a]) g.w = (along < g.len - 0.01) and IRREGULAR_SHORT or 1 end end for i, id in ipairs(order) do fx[id], fy[id] = px[i], py[i] end
for _, id in ipairs(order) do lastFit[id] = { fx[id], fy[id] } end
-- Snap to the grid, nearest the root first. local pos, taken = {}, {} for _, id in ipairs(order) do local x, y = math.floor(fx[id] + 0.5), math.floor(fy[id] + 0.5) if taken[x .. "," .. y] then local best, bestDist = nil, nil for r = 1, 4 do for ddy = -r, r do for ddx = -r, r do local cx, cy = x + ddx, y + ddy if not taken[cx .. "," .. cy] then local dist = (cx - fx[id]) ^ 2 + (cy - fy[id]) ^ 2 if not bestDist or dist < bestDist then best, bestDist = { cx, cy }, dist end end end end if best then break end end if best then x, y = best[1], best[2] end end taken[x .. "," .. y] = id pos[id] = { x, y } end
-- A room sitting on a long exit's line (an exit stretched past it) moves -- to the nearest free cell off every such line, so no exit seems to lead -- into it. local function onLines() local cells = {} for _, e in ipairs(edges) do local pa, pb = pos[e[1]], pos[e[2]] local sx, sy = pb[1] - pa[1], pb[2] - pa[2] local k = math.max(math.abs(sx), math.abs(sy)) if k >= 2 and (sx == 0 or sy == 0 or math.abs(sx) == math.abs(sy)) then for j = 1, k - 1 do cells[(pa[1] + j * sx / k) .. "," .. (pa[2] + j * sy / k)] = true end end end return cells end for _ = 1, 3 do local cells = onLines() local movedAny = false for _, id in ipairs(order) do local p = pos[id] local key = p[1] .. "," .. p[2] if cells[key] then local best, bestDist = nil, nil for r = 1, 3 do for ddy = -r, r do for ddx = -r, r do local cx, cy = p[1] + ddx, p[2] + ddy local ck = cx .. "," .. cy if not taken[ck] and not cells[ck] then local dist = (cx - fx[id]) ^ 2 + (cy - fy[id]) ^ 2 if not bestDist or dist < bestDist then best, bestDist = { cx, cy }, dist end end end end if best then break end end if best then taken[key] = nil taken[best[1] .. "," .. best[2]] = id pos[id] = best movedAny = true end end end if not movedAny then break end end
-- Exits of unrelated rooms shouldn't cross. Each room on a crossing tries -- the free cells around it, and moves where crossings plus the cost of -- bending its own exits (as above) come out lowest; a crossing costs -- more than a slightly bent exit. local byRoom = {} for k, e in ipairs(edges) do byRoom[e[1]] = byRoom[e[1]] or {} byRoom[e[2]] = byRoom[e[2]] or {} byRoom[e[1]][#byRoom[e[1]] + 1] = k byRoom[e[2]][#byRoom[e[2]] + 1] = k end local function crosses(k1, k2) local a, b, c, d = edges[k1][1], edges[k1][2], edges[k2][1], edges[k2][2] if a == c or a == d or b == c or b == d then return false end local p1, p2, p3, p4 = pos[a], pos[b], pos[c], pos[d] local function orient(p, q, r) local v = (q[1] - p[1]) * (r[2] - p[2]) - (q[2] - p[2]) * (r[1] - p[1]) return v > 0 and 1 or (v < 0 and -1 or 0) end local o1, o2 = orient(p1, p2, p3), orient(p1, p2, p4) local o3, o4 = orient(p3, p4, p1), orient(p3, p4, p2) if o1 ~= o2 and o3 ~= o4 and o1 ~= 0 and o2 ~= 0 and o3 ~= 0 and o4 ~= 0 then return true end -- Running along the same line, overlapping. if o1 == 0 and o2 == 0 then local function within(p, q, r) return math.min(p[1], q[1]) <= r[1] and r[1] <= math.max(p[1], q[1]) and math.min(p[2], q[2]) <= r[2] and r[2] <= math.max(p[2], q[2]) end return within(p1, p2, p3) or within(p1, p2, p4) or within(p3, p4, p1) or within(p3, p4, p2) end return false end local function bendCost(k) local e, g = edges[k], geo[k] local dx, dy = pos[e[2]][1] - pos[e[1]][1], pos[e[2]][2] - pos[e[1]][2] local along = g.ux * dx + g.uy * dy local side = -g.uy * dx + g.ux * dy local c = IRREGULAR_BEND * side * side if along < g.len then c = c + IRREGULAR_BEND * (g.len - along) ^ 2 else c = c + (along - g.len) ^ 2 end return c end -- Strictly between a and b on the line joining them. local function onSegment(p, a, b) if (b[1] - a[1]) * (p[2] - a[2]) ~= (b[2] - a[2]) * (p[1] - a[1]) then return false end local t = ((p[1] - a[1]) * (b[1] - a[1]) + (p[2] - a[2]) * (b[2] - a[2])) local len2 = (b[1] - a[1]) ^ 2 + (b[2] - a[2]) ^ 2 return t > 0 and t < len2 end local function roomCost(id) local c = 0 local mine = {} for _, k in ipairs(byRoom[id] or {}) do mine[k] = true c = c + bendCost(k) for k2 = 1, #edges do if k2 ~= k and crosses(k, k2) then c = c + IRREGULAR_CROSS end end -- Another room sitting on this exit's line. local a, b = pos[edges[k][1]], pos[edges[k][2]] for _, other in ipairs(order) do if other ~= edges[k][1] and other ~= edges[k][2] and onSegment(pos[other], a, b) then c = c + IRREGULAR_ON_LINE end end end -- This room sitting on another exit's line. for k2, e in ipairs(edges) do if not mine[k2] and onSegment(pos[id], pos[e[1]], pos[e[2]]) then c = c + IRREGULAR_ON_LINE end end return c end -- A room needing a look: its exits cross others, or a room sits on one -- of them, or it sits on another exit's line. local function troubled(id) for _, k in ipairs(byRoom[id]) do for k2 = 1, #edges do if k2 ~= k and crosses(k, k2) then return true end end local a, b = pos[edges[k][1]], pos[edges[k][2]] for _, other in ipairs(order) do if other ~= edges[k][1] and other ~= edges[k][2] and onSegment(pos[other], a, b) then return true end end end for _, e in ipairs(edges) do if e[1] ~= id and e[2] ~= id and onSegment(pos[id], pos[e[1]], pos[e[2]]) then return true end end return false end for _ = 1, 8 do local improved = false for _, id in ipairs(order) do if id ~= rootId and byRoom[id] then local here = roomCost(id) if troubled(id) then local p0 = pos[id] local best, bestCost = nil, here for ddy = -2, 2 do for ddx = -2, 2 do local cx, cy = p0[1] + ddx, p0[2] + ddy local key = cx .. "," .. cy if not taken[key] then pos[id] = { cx, cy } local c = roomCost(id) if c < bestCost - 0.001 then best, bestCost = { cx, cy }, c end end end end pos[id] = p0 if best then taken[p0[1] .. "," .. p0[2]] = nil taken[best[1] .. "," .. best[2]] = id pos[id] = best improved = true end end end end if not improved then break end end return pos, order end
-- Positions relative to startId (at 0,0), from its area's kept layout. local function LayoutIrregular(startId) local cached = irregularCache[startId] if not cached or cached.version ~= mapVersion or not cached.pos[startId] then local pos, members = SolveIrregular(startId) cached = { version = mapVersion, pos = pos } for _, id in ipairs(members) do irregularCache[id] = cached end end local o = cached.pos[startId] local out = {} for id, p in pairs(cached.pos) do out[id] = { p[1] - o[1], p[2] - o[2] } end return out end
-- Joining pieces of one area mapped from different entrances. -- -- After a new room is created, the rooms laid out around it are compared -- with the rooms laid out around each already-mapped room in the square -- that looks the same but isn't connected to it. A candidate fits when every -- position the two layouts share holds the same room (by name or -- description and exits) and the squares still line up. It's accepted when -- it's the only room like this nearby and a neighbour agrees, or when at -- least JOIN_MIN_MATCHES neighbours agree and one of them is distinctive -- -- and only if exactly one candidate fits. Then every pair of rooms the two -- layouts share is merged, so the pieces become one map. -- Wide enough to cover a whole area like Burnham Wood (about 11 x 11), so -- a contradiction anywhere in the overlap blocks a join, not just nearby. local JOIN_RADIUS = 15 local JOIN_MIN_MATCHES = 2
local function SameRoom(a, b) return Recognised(a, b) and Recognised(b, a) end
-- Returns the number of rooms merged (0 if nothing was joined). -- True if no other room in the room's square looks the same: a corner, an -- edge room with an odd exit, the castle. In a grid of look-alike rooms, -- matching only look-alikes proves nothing, so a join needs one of these. -- -- "Unique among the rooms mapped so far" isn't enough: the first "Burnham -- Wood (n,e,s,w)" mapped in a square is unique there until the next one is. -- So look-alikes in the neighbouring squares count too. Rooms in ignore (the -- piece being joined, which holds this room's own copy) don't. local function Distinctive(room, ignore) for _, other in pairs(rooms) do if other ~= room and not (ignore and ignore[other.id]) and other.sx and other.sy and room.sx and room.sy and math.abs(other.sx - room.sx) <= 1 and math.abs(other.sy - room.sy) <= 1 and SameRoom(other, room) then return false end end return true end
-- Every grid row of a consistent map lies in one row of squares, and every -- grid column in one column of squares. Checks that still holds with the -- two layouts laid over each other (cellB shifted onto posA's frame). local function SquaresConsistent(posA, cellB) local rowY, colX = {}, {} local function add(room, x, y) if room.sy ~= nil then if rowY[y] ~= nil and rowY[y] ~= room.sy then return false end rowY[y] = room.sy end if room.sx ~= nil then if colX[x] ~= nil and colX[x] ~= room.sx then return false end colX[x] = room.sx end return true end for id, p in pairs(posA) do if not add(rooms[id], p[1], p[2]) then return false end end for key, id in pairs(cellB) do local x, y = key:match("^(-?%d+),(-?%d+)$") if not add(rooms[id], tonumber(x), tonumber(y)) then return false end end return true end
-- Two rooms are only the same room if their exits agree: an exit both have -- must lead to the same place -- the same room, or rooms that line up on the -- two overlaid layouts (those get merged too). This catches what the layout -- can't see, like exits out to overland tiles: two entrance roads with the -- same name, one whose south exit leads out of town and one whose south exit -- leads to a street. function ExitsAgree(pairs_, posA, posB) for _, pair in ipairs(pairs_) do local la, lb = links[pair[1]] or {}, links[pair[2]] or {} for cmd, linkA in pairs(la) do local linkB = lb[cmd] if linkB and linkA.to ~= linkB.to then local pa, pb = posA[linkA.to], posB[linkB.to] if not (pa and pb and pa[1] == pb[1] and pa[2] == pb[2]) then return false end end end end return true end
-- Returns the pairs to merge for each candidate that fits. local function TryJoinByGrid(roomId) local room = rooms[roomId] local posA = Layout(roomId, JOIN_RADIUS, true)
local candidates = {} for _, cand in pairs(rooms) do if not posA[cand.id] and SameSquare(cand, room.sx, room.sy) and SameRoom(cand, room) then candidates[#candidates + 1] = cand end end local fits = {} if #candidates == 0 then return fits end
for _, cand in ipairs(candidates) do local posB, cellB = Layout(cand.id, JOIN_RADIUS, true) local pairs_, matches, distinctive, ok = { { roomId, cand.id } }, 0, false, true for id, p in pairs(posA) do if id ~= roomId then local other = cellB[p[1] .. "," .. p[2]] if other then if posA[other] then ok = false; break end -- already connected if SameRoom(rooms[id], rooms[other]) then matches = matches + 1 pairs_[#pairs_ + 1] = { id, other } if not distinctive and Distinctive(rooms[other], posA) then distinctive = true end elseif not Compatible(rooms[other], rooms[id]) then ok = false break end end end end ok = ok and SquaresConsistent(posA, cellB) and ExitsAgree(pairs_, posA, posB) -- Even a distinctive room needs one neighbour to agree: "the only one -- like it mapped so far" doesn't mean the only one there is. local enough = (#candidates == 1 and matches >= 1 and (distinctive or Distinctive(cand, posA))) or (matches >= JOIN_MIN_MATCHES and distinctive) if ok and enough then fits[#fits + 1] = pairs_ end end return fits end
-- Irregular squares: the grid can't tell two look-alikes apart, and coming -- back around an uneven loop lands you in a room the grid puts somewhere -- else, so it gets mapped twice. Copies like that are found by the paths -- between rooms instead: from the new room and from a look-alike, follow -- the same commands side by side. Every pair of rooms reached that way must -- look the same (or at least not contradict), no room may pair up with two -- different rooms, and the two sides may not run into each other. Each -- pair that really looks the same, and each exit on both sides that leads -- to the very same room, is a neighbour that agrees. local PATH_JOIN_LIMIT = 60 -- pairs followed at most per candidate
-- Returns the pairs and how many neighbours agree, or nil on a contradiction. local function MatchByPath(a, b) local mapAB, mapBA = { [a] = b }, { [b] = a } local pairs_, matches = { { a, b } }, 0 local head = 1 while pairs_[head] and #pairs_ <= PATH_JOIN_LIMIT do local x, y = pairs_[head][1], pairs_[head][2] head = head + 1 for cmd, lx in pairs(links[x] or {}) do local ly = links[y] and links[y][cmd] local p, q = lx.to, ly and ly.to if q and rooms[p] and rooms[q] then if p == q then matches = matches + 1 -- both lead to the same room elseif mapAB[p] or mapBA[q] then if mapAB[p] ~= q then return nil end -- paired with something else elseif mapBA[p] or mapAB[q] then return nil -- the two sides run together elseif SameRoom(rooms[p], rooms[q]) then matches = matches + 1 mapAB[p], mapBA[q] = q, p pairs_[#pairs_ + 1] = { p, q } elseif not Compatible(rooms[q], rooms[p]) then return nil end end end end return pairs_, matches, mapAB end
local function TryJoinByPath(roomId) local room = rooms[roomId] local fits = {} for _, cand in pairs(rooms) do if cand ~= room and SameSquare(cand, room.sx, room.sy) and SameRoom(cand, room) then local pairs_, matches, aSide = MatchByPath(roomId, cand.id) if pairs_ and matches >= 1 then -- The same rule as on a grid: a neighbour must agree, and something -- must be the only one like it (not counting this side's copies). local distinctive = Distinctive(cand, aSide) for i = 2, #pairs_ do if distinctive then break end distinctive = Distinctive(rooms[pairs_[i][2]], aSide) end if distinctive then fits[#fits + 1] = pairs_ end end end end return fits end
function TryJoin(roomId) local room = rooms[roomId] if not room or IsOverland(room) then return 0 end local fits = IsIrregular(room.sx, room.sy) and TryJoinByPath(roomId) or TryJoinByGrid(roomId) if #fits ~= 1 then return 0 end
for _, pair in ipairs(fits[1]) do local drop, keep = rooms[pair[1]], rooms[pair[2]] if drop and keep and drop ~= keep then MergeRooms(keep, drop) end end return #fits[1] end
-- On a grid, a room mapped twice that the paths between rooms could prove -- (but the grid can't) means the area doesn't fit a grid: say so, once per -- square per session. local suggested = {}
function SuggestIrregular(roomId) local room = rooms[roomId] if not room or IsOverland(room) then return end local label = SquareLabel(room.sx, room.sy) if suggested[label] or IsIrregular(room.sx, room.sy) then return end local fits = TryJoinByPath(roomId) if #fits ~= 1 then return end -- Only a copy you can walk to from the original without leaving the -- area: pieces mapped from different entrances aren't connected yet, and -- the grid joins those. local cand = fits[1][1][2] local seen, queue, head = { [roomId] = true }, { roomId }, 1 while queue[head] and not seen[cand] and #queue < 500 do for _, link in pairs(links[queue[head]] or {}) do if rooms[link.to] and not seen[link.to] and not IsOverland(rooms[link.to]) then seen[link.to] = true queue[#queue + 1] = link.to end end head = head + 1 end if seen[cand] then suggested[label] = true Note("room #" .. roomId .. " looks like one already mapped, which the grid puts elsewhere: this area's " .. "rooms probably don't line up on a grid. If the map shows rooms twice here, type 'amap irregular'.") end end
-- Every room in an irregular square, until nothing more joins: a copy made -- on an uneven loop can be proven only later, when a walk elsewhere gives -- it and the original an exit in common. local function JoinSquare(sx, sy) local merged = 0 for _ = 1, 5 do local list = {} for _, room in pairs(rooms) do if SameSquare(room, sx, sy) then list[#list + 1] = room end end table.sort(list, function(a, b) return a.id < b.id end) -- Only rooms with a look-alike in the square can be copies. local ids = {} for i, a in ipairs(list) do for j, b in ipairs(list) do if i ~= j and SameRoom(a, b) then ids[#ids + 1] = a.id break end end end local pass = 0 for _, id in ipairs(ids) do if rooms[id] then pass = pass + TryJoin(id) end end merged = merged + pass if pass == 0 then break end end return merged end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Reading a block of output -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- "north, east and west" / "east" -> list of short directions (or words). local function ParseExitList(text) text = text:gsub("%.%s*$", ""):gsub(" and ", ",") local list = {} for word in text:gmatch("[^,]+") do word = Trim(word):lower() if word ~= "" then list[#list + 1] = DIR_WORDS[word] or word end end return list end
-- Pulls "There is a closed gate leading west [and an open door leading -- east]." out of a description, returning the cleaned text and the doors. local function ExtractDoors(desc) local doors = {} local cleaned = desc:gsub("There is ([^%.]- leading [^%.]-)%.%s*", function(body) local found = false for clause in (body .. " and "):gmatch("(.-) and ") do local state, dirWord = clause:match("^an? (%a+) .- leading (%a+)$") local dir = dirWord and DIR_WORDS[dirWord:lower()] if dir and (state == "open" or state == "closed") then doors[dir] = (state == "closed") found = true end end if found then return "" end end) return Trim(cleaned), doors end
local function NewObs(mode) return { mode = mode, exits = {}, doors = {}, items = {} } end
local function CopyItems(obs, lines, from) for i = from, #lines do obs.items[#obs.items + 1] = lines[i] end end
local function FinishVerbose(obs, descLines) -- A short first line in a multi-line description is a message printed -- before the room ("You jump down."): wrapped description lines are -- nearly full width. while #descLines > 1 and #descLines[1] < 60 do table.remove(descLines, 1) end local desc, doors = ExtractDoors(CollapseSpaces(table.concat(descLines, " "))) if desc ~= "" then obs.desc = desc end for d, closed in pairs(doors) do obs.doors[d] = closed obs.exits[d] = true end return obs end
local function ParseBrief(name, text) local obs = NewObs("brief") obs.name = name if text == "no exits" then return obs end for token in text:gmatch("[^,]+") do token = Trim(token) local inner = token:match("^|(.*)|$") local word = (inner or token):lower() local dir = DIR_WORDS[word] or word obs.exits[dir] = true if inner then obs.doors[dir] = true end end return obs end
-- Returns obs, or nil plus "fail" and the failure line. local function ParseBlock(lines) -- Verbose: find the exits line. for i, line in ipairs(lines) do local exitsText, itemsFrom local rest = line:match("^%s*Obvious directions are:%s*(.-)%s*$") if rest then local parts = { rest } local j = i while not parts[#parts]:match("%.$") and lines[j + 1] do j = j + 1 parts[#parts + 1] = Trim(lines[j]) end exitsText, itemsFrom = table.concat(parts, " "), j + 1 else local one = line:match("^%s*The only obvious exit is (.-)%.?%s*$") if one then exitsText, itemsFrom = one, i + 1 elseif line:match("^%s*There are no obvious exits") then exitsText, itemsFrom = "", i + 1 end end if exitsText then local obs = NewObs("verbose") for _, e in ipairs(ParseExitList(exitsText)) do obs.exits[e] = true end local descLines = {} for k = 1, i - 1 do descLines[#descLines + 1] = lines[k] end CopyItems(obs, lines, itemsFrom) return FinishVerbose(obs, descLines) end end
-- Brief: "Room Name (n,e,|w|,se)". for i, line in ipairs(lines) do local name, text = line:match("^(%S.-) %(([^()]*)%)$") if name and ValidBriefExits(text) then local obs = ParseBrief(name, text) CopyItems(obs, lines, i + 1) return obs end end
-- Dark: no name, no description, no exits -- only the path tells where. for i, line in ipairs(lines) do for _, pattern in ipairs(DARK_PATTERNS) do if line:match(pattern) then local obs = NewObs("dark") obs.dark = true CopyItems(obs, lines, i + 1) return obs end end end
for _, line in ipairs(lines) do for _, pattern in ipairs(FAILURE_PATTERNS) do if line:match(pattern) then return nil, "fail", line end end end return nil end
-- Verbose room with no exits line at all (every exit behind a closed door). -- Only tried after a direction or look, since it's a guess: the description -- runs on while the previous line was near full width. It must contain a -- "There is a closed ... leading ..." sentence -- that's the only way a room -- ends up with no exits line -- so a long message that wraps (an NPC -- blocking you) isn't mistaken for a room. local function ParseLooseVerbose(lines) if #lines == 0 then return nil end local descLines = { lines[1] } local i = 2 while lines[i] and #lines[i - 1] >= 60 do descLines[#descLines + 1] = lines[i] i = i + 1 end local obs = FinishVerbose(NewObs("verbose"), descLines) if not next(obs.doors) then return nil end CopyItems(obs, lines, i) return obs end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Commands you send -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Returns kind ("move", "look", "nonmove", "other" or nil) and the exit key. -- Game aliases --------------------------------------------------------------
local function SaveGameWord(kind, name, expansion) gameWords[kind][name] = expansion if expansion then DbRun("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO game_words (kind, name, expansion) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", kind, name, expansion) else DbRun("DELETE FROM game_words WHERE kind = ? AND name = ?", kind, name) end end
-- Fills in an alias's $ arguments: $1..$9 one word each, $* everything, -- $ the first word and $@ the words after it (or everything when there's -- no $). Without any, the words go on the end. local function FillArgs(template, args) local words = {} for w in args:gmatch("%S+") do words[#words + 1] = w end local usedDollar = template:find("%$[^%d%*@]") or template:find("%$$") local used = false local out = template:gsub("%$([%d%*@]?)", function(c) used = true if c == "*" then return args end if c == "@" then return usedDollar and table.concat(words, " ", 2) or args end if c == "" then return words[1] or "" end return words[tonumber(c)] or "" end) if not used and args ~= "" then out = out .. " " .. args end return CollapseSpaces(out) end
local function ApplyNicks(cmd) local first = cmd:match("^(%S+)") if first == "alias" or first == "nick" or first == "unalias" or first == "unnick" then return cmd end return (cmd:gsub("%S+", function(w) return gameWords.nick[w] or w end)) end
-- What a typed line really sends, as a list of commands: aliases expanded -- (">name" inside one calls another alias), "do a, b" split up, nicknames -- replaced. Definitions sent along the way are learned. local function ExpandCommand(text, depth, out) out = out or {} depth = depth or 0 text = CollapseSpaces(text) if depth > 6 or text == "" then return out end local first, args = text:match("^(%S+)%s*(.*)$") local template = gameWords.alias[first] if template then text = FillArgs(template, args) if text:sub(1, 1) == ">" then return ExpandCommand(text:sub(2), depth + 1, out) end end if text:match("^do ") then for part in (text:sub(4) .. ","):gmatch("%s*([^,]-)%s*,") do if part:sub(1, 1) == ">" then part = part:sub(2) end -- Each part of a "do" goes through the alias table again. ExpandCommand(part, depth + 1, out) end return out end text = ApplyNicks(text) local kind, name, expansion = nil, nil, nil name, expansion = text:match("^alias (%S+) (.+)$") if name then kind = "alias" else name, expansion = text:match("^nick (%S+) (.+)$") if name then kind = "nick" end end if kind then SaveGameWord(kind, name, expansion) end out[#out + 1] = text return out end
-- Reading the 'alias' / 'nick' listing ("ep = enter portal"), page -- by page. A complete listing replaces what was known; a cut-short one only -- adds to it. local listing = nil -- { kind =, words = {}, count =, total = }
local function StartListing(kind) listing = { kind = kind, words = {}, count = 0, total = nil } end
-- Hidden exits saved under an alias name ("ep") are renamed to what the -- alias sends ("enter portal"), the name new ones get. local function RenameAliasLinks() for fromId, cmds in pairs(links) do local renames = {} for cmd, link in pairs(cmds) do if not DIRS[cmd] then local list = ExpandCommand(cmd) local real = #list == 1 and CollapseSpaces(list[1]:lower()) or nil if real and real ~= cmd and not DIRS[real] and not cmds[real] then renames[cmd] = real end end end for cmd, real in pairs(renames) do local link = cmds[cmd] cmds[cmd] = nil DbRun("DELETE FROM exits WHERE from_id = ? AND cmd = ?", fromId, cmd) SetLink(fromId, real, link.to, link.hidden) end end end
local function FinishListing() local l = listing listing = nil if l.count == 0 then return end if l.total == nil or l.count >= l.total then for name in pairs(gameWords[l.kind]) do if not l.words[name] then SaveGameWord(l.kind, name, nil) end end end for name, expansion in pairs(l.words) do SaveGameWord(l.kind, name, expansion) end RenameAliasLinks() mapChanged = true Note("learned " .. l.count .. " game " .. (l.kind == "alias" and "aliases" or "nicknames") .. " (commands are read through them, e.g. an alias for 'enter portal').") end
-- Returns true if the line belongs to the listing. local function ListingLine(text) if not listing then return false end local more, total = text:match("^%-%-More%-%-%((%d+)/(%d+)%)") if more then listing.total = tonumber(total) return true end if Trim(text) == "" then return true end local name, expansion = text:match("^(%S+) +=%s(.*)$") if name then if not listing.words[name] then listing.count = listing.count + 1 end listing.words[name] = Trim(expansion) return true end FinishListing() return false end
local ClassifyOne
-- A typed line through the game's aliases. A line that sends several -- commands counts as a move only if one of them could move you, and keeps -- what you typed as its name (it's what would be sent again). local function Classify(cmd) if not cmd then return nil end local list = ExpandCommand(cmd) if #list == 0 then return nil end if #list == 1 then return ClassifyOne(list[1]) end for _, part in ipairs(list) do local kind = ClassifyOne(part) if kind == "move" or kind == "other" then return "other", CollapseSpaces(cmd:lower()) end end return "nonmove" end
function ClassifyOne(cmd) local t = CollapseSpaces(cmd:lower()) if t == "" then return nil end if DIR_WORDS[t] then return "move", DIR_WORDS[t] end if LOOK_WORDS[t] then return "look" end local first = t:match("^(%S+)") if PEER_WORDS[first] then return "peer" end if NON_MOVE_VERBS[first] or LOOK_WORDS[first] or first:match("^['\":]") then return "nonmove" end return "other", t end
function OnPluginSent(text) -- Paging on through "--More--" gets no prompt of its own. if pagerActive then pagerActive = false return end local expanded = ExpandCommand(text) if #expanded == 1 and (expanded[1] == "alias" or expanded[1] == "nick") then StartListing(expanded[1]) end -- A move that got no reply yet is only kept while nothing newer was sent. for i = #cmdQueue, 1, -1 do if cmdQueue[i].requeued then table.remove(cmdQueue, i) end end cmdQueue[#cmdQueue + 1] = { text = text, t = os.time() } if #cmdQueue > 20 then table.remove(cmdQueue, 1) end end
local function PopCommand() local now = os.time() while cmdQueue[1] and now - cmdQueue[1].t > 10 do table.remove(cmdQueue, 1) end return table.remove(cmdQueue, 1) end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Following you around -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
local function Arrive(room) StampRoom(room) current = room.id lastKnown = room.id lostCount = 0 -- Kept up to date (not only when MUSHclient saves state), so a reload -- can pick up where you were. SetVariable("last_room", tostring(room.id)) end
-- After a reload (or a new session) the plugin doesn't know where you are, -- but you're most likely still in the last room it saw you in. That room -- is taken back on the first room you see, if it fits: you look and it's -- that room, or you move by an exit it has and land where that exit is -- known to lead (or, for an exit not taken yet, in the same or a -- neighbouring square). Otherwise you're found the usual way. local resumeId = nil
local function TryResume(kind, key, obs, sx, sy) local r = resumeId and rooms[resumeId] resumeId = nil if not r or current then return false end local fits = false if kind == "look" or kind == "nonmove" or kind == nil then fits = Recognised(r, obs) elseif kind == "move" or kind == "other" then local link = links[r.id] and links[r.id][key] if link and rooms[link.to] then local to = rooms[link.to] fits = SameSquare(to, sx, sy) and Recognised(to, obs) elseif r.exits[key] and r.sx and r.sy and sx and sy then fits = math.abs(r.sx - sx) <= 1 and math.abs(r.sy - sy) <= 1 end end if fits then current = r.id end return fits end
-- No path to go by: find the room by its text within the current square. -- exclude: a room it can't be (the one you just left). local function Relocate(obs, sx, sy, exclude) if not obs.name and not obs.desc then current = nil return "position unknown: a room with no name or description can't be recognised" end local matches = {} for _, room in pairs(rooms) do if room ~= exclude and SameSquare(room, sx, sy) and Recognised(room, obs) then matches[#matches + 1] = room end end if #matches == 1 and not Distinctive(matches[1]) and RoomsInSquare(sx, sy) > 1 then -- The only one mapped in this square, but look-alikes are all around: -- it could just as well be an unmapped one. (Not for an overland tile: -- an overland square holds exactly one room, so a match there is certain.) current = nil lostCount = 1 return "lost: looks like room #" .. matches[1].id .. ", but rooms like it are common here" elseif #matches == 1 then UpdateRoom(matches[1], obs) Arrive(matches[1]) return "recognised room #" .. matches[1].id elseif #matches == 0 then local room = NewRoom(obs, sx, sy) Arrive(room) return "new room #" .. room.id .. " (not linked: no move to go by)" end current = nil lostCount = #matches return "lost: " .. #matches .. " rooms in this square look like this" end
local function FollowMove(prev, kind, key, obs, sx, sy) local link = links[prev.id] and links[prev.id][key] local target, how
if link and rooms[link.to] then local cand = rooms[link.to] -- Descriptions can change (weather, time of day), so a known exit only -- needs the exits and name to agree. -- A room never changes square, so if the game reports a different -- one, the stored exit is wrong. if SameSquare(cand, sx, sy) and ExitsCompatible(cand, obs) and NameCompatible(cand, obs) then target, how = cand, "followed known exit to room #" .. cand.id if link.build ~= BUILD then link.build = BUILD SaveLink(prev.id, key, link) end end end
-- Overland tiles are left out of the layout: one overland step spans a -- whole area, so grid positions measured through them mean nothing. local pos, cellAt = Layout(prev.id, 12, true)
-- (Not in an irregular square, where the grid spot proves nothing.) if not target and kind == "move" and DIRS[key].dx and not IsIrregular(sx, sy) then local cid = cellAt[DIRS[key].dx .. "," .. DIRS[key].dy] local cand = cid and rooms[cid] -- In the dark, the grid position is all there is to go by. if cand and SameSquare(cand, sx, sy) and (Recognised(cand, obs) or (obs.dark and cand.dark)) then target, how = cand, "closed a loop into room #" .. cand.id end end
if not target and kind == "move" then -- A look-alike whose exit back towards you already leads to exactly the -- room you came from is the room you're in (e.g. stepping back into an -- entrance from the overland tile it leads out to). local rev = DIRS[key].rev local back = nil for _, cand in pairs(rooms) do local l = links[cand.id] and links[cand.id][rev] if cand ~= prev and l and l.to == prev.id and SameSquare(cand, sx, sy) and (Recognised(cand, obs) or (obs.dark and cand.dark)) then if back then back = false; break end back = cand end end if back then target, how = back, "recognised room #" .. back.id .. " (its exit back leads to where you came from)" end end
-- (Coming into a part of an area mapped from another entrance is left to -- TryJoin: a room that's merely the only one like it mapped so far -- the -- first "Main Street (n,e,s,w)" of two in a town -- isn't evidence on its -- own, so a join needs a neighbour that agrees as well.)
if not target and kind == "move" and RoomsInSquare(sx, sy) == 1 and not SameSquare(prev, sx, sy) then -- Stepping onto an overland tile you've been on before, from a side -- you haven't come from yet. for _, cand in pairs(rooms) do if SameSquare(cand, sx, sy) then if Recognised(cand, obs) then target, how = cand, "recognised overland room #" .. cand.id end break end end end
if not target then -- Going back the way you came, by an exit that doesn't mirror the one -- you took (e.g. "u" out of a pit you entered with "jump down"). -- Compass ways in are left out: those already get a reverse link, and -- look-alike rooms in a row (Main Street, Main Street) are common. local back = {} for fromId, cmds in pairs(links) do if rooms[fromId] and SameSquare(rooms[fromId], sx, sy) then for cmd, l in pairs(cmds) do local planar = DIRS[cmd] and DIRS[cmd].dx if l.to == prev.id and not planar and Recognised(rooms[fromId], obs) then back[fromId] = true end end end end local only = next(back) if only and next(back, only) == nil then target, how = rooms[only], "went back to room #" .. only end end
if not target and link then -- The known exit led somewhere unexpected: trust what just happened -- over the old link. local result = Relocate(obs, sx, sy, prev) -- Correct the exit only within the same square. An exit into another -- square that the game contradicts more likely means the room you were -- in was misidentified than that the exit is wrong. if current and current ~= prev.id and SameSquare(rooms[link.to], sx, sy) then SetLink(prev.id, key, current, link.hidden) return result .. " (exit '" .. key .. "' led somewhere else; exit corrected)" end return result .. " (exit '" .. key .. "' didn't lead where expected)" end
if not target and kind == "other" and not prev.exits[key] and not obs.dark then -- An unlisted command that lands in a known room: if it's nearby (same -- or neighbouring square), it's a hidden exit like "ep" back out of a -- portal; if it's far away, it's a teleport (recall, a spell), so arrive -- there without saving an exit. local before = current local result = Relocate(obs, sx, sy) local here = current and rooms[current] local near = here and prev.sx and prev.sy and here.sx and here.sy and math.abs(prev.sx - here.sx) <= 1 and math.abs(prev.sy - here.sy) <= 1 if here and result:match("^recognised") then if not near or TELEPORT_WORDS[key:match("^(%S+)")] then return result .. " (via '" .. key .. "', a teleport: not saved as an exit)" end SetLink(prev.id, key, here.id, true) return result .. " (via hidden exit '" .. key .. "')" end -- Relocate created a new room (or got lost); a new room after an -- unlisted command is a hidden exit -- unless it's far away (a blue -- door from Tantallon to Drakhiya, 37 squares off) or a teleport. if current and current ~= before and (not near or TELEPORT_WORDS[key:match("^(%S+)")]) then return result .. " (via '" .. key .. "', a teleport: not saved as an exit)" end if current and current ~= before then target = rooms[current] how = "new room #" .. target.id .. " (hidden exit '" .. key .. "')" else return result end end
if not target then target = NewRoom(obs, sx, sy) how = "new room #" .. target.id end
UpdateRoom(target, obs) if prev.noexits and prev.noexits[key] then prev.noexits[key] = nil -- it was blocked before (a door, a guard), but it is an exit SaveRoom(prev) end -- A dark room's exits are unknown, so a compass move out of one isn't hidden. SetLink(prev.id, key, target.id, not (prev.exits[key] or (prev.dark and DIRS[key]))) local rev = DIRS[key] and DIRS[key].rev -- The way back is assumed: listed in the new room, or the new room is dark -- (no exits to check, and the path is all there is to go by). if rev and (target.exits[rev] or target.dark) and not (links[target.id] and links[target.id][rev]) then SetLink(target.id, rev, prev.id, false) end Arrive(target) return how end
local function StripPrompt(lines) if not promptSpec then -- Only the broadcast line itself is known to be part of the prompt. table.remove(lines) return end local last = promptSpec.last local function matches(line, idx) return line and promptSpec.regexes[idx]:match(line) ~= nil end local n = #lines local all = true for k = 1, last do if not matches(lines[n - last + k], k) then all = false; break end end if all then for _ = 1, last do table.remove(lines) end else table.remove(lines) end skipLines = #promptSpec.regexes - last end
local function FetchPromptSpec() if not IsPluginInstalled(WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ID) then return end local _, text = CallPlugin(WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ID, "MW_GetPromptLines") if type(text) ~= "string" or text == "" then promptSpec = nil if not warnedNoPrompt then warnedNoPrompt = true Note("mush_windows hasn't read your prompt yet -- type wf_prompt_setup.") end return end local parts = {} for line in (text .. "\n"):gmatch("(.-)\n") do parts[#parts + 1] = line end local last = tonumber(table.remove(parts)) local regexes = {} for i, pattern in ipairs(parts) do local ok, re = pcall(rex.new, pattern) if not ok then Note("couldn't use prompt line " .. i .. " (" .. tostring(re) .. ").") promptSpec = nil return end regexes[i] = re end promptSpec = { regexes = regexes, last = last or #regexes } end
local function ProcessBlock(sx, sy) local lines = {} for _, line in ipairs(buffer) do line = line:gsub("%s+$", "") if line ~= "" then lines[#lines + 1] = line end end buffer = {} StripPrompt(lines)
local entry = PopCommand() local cmd = entry and entry.text local kind, key = Classify(cmd) local obs, status, failLine = ParseBlock(lines) if not obs and not status and (kind == "move" or kind == "look") then obs = ParseLooseVerbose(lines) end
local debug = { cmd = cmd, kind = kind, key = key, lines = lines, obs = obs, sx = sx, sy = sy } lastDebug = debug
if not obs then if status == "fail" then debug.failLine = failLine debug.decision = "move failed: " .. failLine -- In a dark room, a failed move is the only way to learn its exits: -- remember the direction as "no exit". A closed door or a guard in -- the way doesn't count. local here = current and rooms[current] if kind == "move" and here and here.dark and not failLine:match("^The .+ is closed%.$") and not failLine:match(" stops you from going ") then here.noexits = here.noexits or {} if not here.noexits[key] then here.noexits[key] = true SaveRoom(here) debug.decision = debug.decision .. " (no exit '" .. key .. "' noted for dark room #" .. here.id .. ")" mapChanged = true end end else debug.decision = "no room in this output" -- A move whose reply hasn't arrived yet (e.g. a combat round's prompt -- came first): keep it for the next prompt, unless more was sent. if kind == "move" and #cmdQueue == 0 and os.time() - entry.t <= 3 and not entry.requeued then entry.requeued = true table.insert(cmdQueue, 1, entry) debug.decision = debug.decision .. " (kept the move for the next prompt)" end end return false end
if kind == "peer" then debug.decision = "looked into another room ('" .. tostring(cmd) .. "'): not where you are" return false end
local resumed = TryResume(kind, key, obs, sx, sy) local prev = current and rooms[current]
if kind == "look" or kind == "nonmove" or (kind == nil and prev and Compatible(prev, obs)) then if prev and Compatible(prev, obs) then UpdateRoom(prev, obs) debug.decision = "same room #" .. prev.id else debug.decision = Relocate(obs, sx, sy) end elseif kind == "other" and prev and Recognised(prev, obs) then UpdateRoom(prev, obs) debug.decision = "same room #" .. prev.id .. " ('" .. key .. "' didn't move you)" elseif prev and (kind == "move" or kind == "other") then debug.decision = FollowMove(prev, kind, key, obs, sx, sy) else debug.decision = Relocate(obs, sx, sy) end if resumed then debug.decision = debug.decision .. " (picked up from room #" .. prev.id .. ", where you were before the reload)" end return true end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- Plugin callbacks -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function OnPluginLineReceived(text) if skipLines > 0 then -- Only skip what really is the rest of the prompt. local idx = #promptSpec.regexes - skipLines + 1 local re = promptSpec.regexes[idx] if re and re:match(text) then skipLines = skipLines - 1 return true end skipLines = 0 end if ListingLine(text) then pagerActive = text:match("^%-%-More%-%-") ~= nil return true end pagerActive = text:match("^%-%-More%-%-") ~= nil buffer[#buffer + 1] = text if #buffer > 300 then table.remove(buffer, 1) end return true end
local function RedrawMap() if mapWin then mapWin:redraw() end end
-- A short "what was seen" for the trace: brief name or the start of the -- description, plus exits. local function SeenSummary(obs) local text = obs.name or (obs.desc and obs.desc:sub(1, 40)) or (obs.dark and "(dark)") or "?" return text .. " (" .. SetToString(obs.exits) .. ")" end
local TRACE_KEEP = 20000
-- Every move (and failed move) goes into the trace table, so what the -- plugin really decided in the client can be read back from area_map.db; -- with 'amap trace' on, it's also printed. function RecordTrace(d, fromId, toId) if not d or not d.cmd and not d.obs then return end local isFail = d.decision and d.decision:match("^move failed") if not d.obs and not isFail then return end local seen = d.obs and SeenSummary(d.obs) or d.failLine DbRun("INSERT INTO trace (t, cmd, from_id, to_id, sq_x, sq_y, seen, decision, build) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), d.cmd, fromId, toId, d.sx, d.sy, seen, d.decision, BUILD) DbRun("DELETE FROM trace WHERE n <= (SELECT MAX(n) FROM trace) - ?", TRACE_KEEP) if traceOn then local text = string.format("[amap] %s: #%s -> #%s @%s %s -- %s", d.cmd or "(no command)", tostring(fromId or "?"), tostring(toId or "?"), SquareLabel(d.sx, d.sy), seen, d.decision or "") ColourNote("gray", "", text) end end
function OnPluginBroadcast(msg, id, name, text) if id ~= WINDOWS_PLUGIN_ID then return end if msg == MW_BROADCAST_PROMPT_CHANGED then warnedNoPrompt = false FetchPromptSpec() elseif msg == MW_BROADCAST_PROMPT then if not promptSpec then FetchPromptSpec() end local sx, sy = (text or ""):match("^(-?%d*),(-?%d*)$") square.x, square.y = tonumber(sx), tonumber(sy) local before = current local t0 = utils.timer() mergeLog = {} mapChanged = false -- One transaction per move: a new room is several writes (room, exit, -- reverse exit), which would otherwise each wait for the disk. db:exec("BEGIN") local idBefore = nextId local happened = ProcessBlock(square.x, square.y) if nextId ~= idBefore then local merged = MergeDuplicatesInSquare(square.x, square.y) if merged > 0 and lastDebug then lastDebug.decision = lastDebug.decision .. " (merged " .. merged .. " duplicate(s) in this square)" end end -- Tried on every move, not only new rooms, so pieces mapped before -- (or by an older version) join up as you walk through them. local joined = (happened and current) and TryJoin(current) or 0 if happened and IsIrregular(square.x, square.y) then joined = joined + JoinSquare(square.x, square.y) elseif happened and joined == 0 and current then SuggestIrregular(current) end if joined > 0 and lastDebug then lastDebug.decision = lastDebug.decision .. (IsIrregular(square.x, square.y) and (" (rooms mapped twice, proven by the paths between them: " .. joined .. " room(s) merged)") or (" (joined onto the part of this area mapped from another entrance: " .. joined .. " room(s) merged)")) end if lastDebug and #mergeLog > 0 then lastDebug.decision = lastDebug.decision .. " [merged " .. table.concat(mergeLog, " ") .. "]" end RecordTrace(lastDebug, before, current) db:exec("COMMIT") local t1 = utils.timer() if happened or before ~= current or mapChanged then -- Only redraw when something happened: a redraw rebuilds every -- hotspot, which would cancel a tooltip the mouse is waiting on. RedrawMap() end if lastDebug then lastDebug.processMs = (t1 - t0) * 1000 lastDebug.drawMs = (utils.timer() - t1) * 1000 end end end
